SMTO-LLM-0052 — The AI model asked for an action without naming it

GUID: 5e16edd8-8349-4385-b4a0-16b09f8567e3
Slug: model-tool-function-missing
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: llm

What happened

  • The model's reply included an action but didn't say which tool to use. SMTO won't guess, so nothing from that reply was run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the steps already shown for this task in the conversation and note which ones finished before the error. Work finished before this reply still stands, so you only need SMTO to continue, not redo it.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing and pick a different model for Main (and Helper, if one is set), then save. Missing tool names come from the model server's output; a different model usually fills them in.
  3. If someone else runs your AI model server, ask them to check that tool calling is turned on and set up for this model. A server without the right tool-calling setting can drop the tool name from the reply.
  4. Send a new message asking SMTO to continue from where it stopped, without repeating the steps that already finished. With a complete reply, SMTO knows exactly which tool to use next.

What success looks like

  • SMTO carries out the model's next action and the task continues without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your AI model server. You don't need to shorten or clear the conversation; this problem isn't caused by its length.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A tool call in the model response lacks its function object or a nonempty function name, so the turn was rejected before dispatch.

What this means

  • A call omits its function object or usable function name, leaving no supported function selection to validate. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • A call omits its function object or usable function name, leaving no supported function selection to validate.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the function object's presence and nonempty exact name; compare with the advertised tool list.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the raw tool_calls from the configured endpoint; every call needs a function object with the exact advertised name and its arguments. Use a serving stack and tool parser that return complete native tool-call records, or route to a compatible endpoint in Settings › Setup › Model routing.
  • Use a serving stack that returns complete native tool-call records, including the advertised function name and arguments.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Each call supplies its supported function object, exact name and valid arguments.

What not to do

  • Do not replay prior successful operations to repair a later model response.
  • Do not disable protocol validation or treat this representation failure as input-context overflow.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
